guitar.evidence: Duane Allman's Gibson Les Paul (and slide work) and Dickey Betts' Gibson Les Paul/SG use are well documented in Southern rock history.

tone.target: raw Southern rock crunch with upper-mid bite
tone.profile: raw Southern rock crunch with upper-mid bite
tone.summary: A gritty signal chain utilizing a Boost/OD for bite, followed by the UK 45 amp model and UK Vintage 4x12 cab, topped off with Chorus and Room ambience.
corrections: drop spring/plate reverb as a focus
replace Fender guess with Marshall/Plexi family
lean more raw and biting than warm

rig.name: The Allman Brothers Band - Whipping Post - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide the necessary upper-mid bite and slight edge of breakup characteristic of Plexi tones.

alternatives.reason: Good alternative for general grit, but Green OD better captures the specific bite needed.

blocks.purpose: Keep the gain structure focused on preamp overdrive rather than heavy distortion.
blocks.gap: The Green OD handles the required grit; adding a dedicated DST unit might over-saturate or muddy the tone.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall Plexi sound required for Southern rock crunch.

alternatives.reason: Similar, but UK 45 is more classically associated with the desired Plexi tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic Marshall-era cabinet voicing.
Slightly boost the upper-mids to enhance bite and cut through a dual guitar mix.
Add subtle movement and width to the tone, enhancing the 'singing sustain' quality.
Provide the requested 'dry room feel' without sounding overly polished or wet.

alternatives.reason: Too bright and artificial for this raw Southern rock tone.

blocks.purpose: Delay is not essential for the core rhythm tone and can clutter the mix.
blocks.gap: The signal chain works well without a dedicated delay unit.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR to better capture raw, biting Marshall Plexi cabinet character.

proposals.reason: Enhance the raw bite and mid-focus of the classic Plexi sound.
